title: Uses of Everyday Materials
seo_title: Year 2 Science: Uses of Everyday Materials Worksheets (Choosing Materials)
standard_text: Identify and compare the suitability of a variety of everyday materials, including wood, metal, plastic, glass, brick, rock, paper and cardboard for particular uses.
meta_desc: Free Year 2 science worksheets on the uses of everyday materials: wood, metal, plastic, glass, brick, rock, paper and cardboard, why they are chosen and a waterproof test. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Choose a material that suits the job.
key_sub: Glass is see-through, metal is strong, plastic is waterproof.
body_html:
How to think about it

We choose materials that suit the job.

  • Glass is see-through, metal is strong, plastic is waterproof.
  • One material can be used for many things.
  • One object can be made of different materials.
Example

Why is a window made of glass?

We need to see through it

Answer: it is transparent

Example

Why not a paper umbrella?

Water soaks in

Answer: paper is not waterproof

Common mistakes

  • Thinking windows are glass only because glass is shiny.
  • Thinking paper would make a good umbrella.
  • Thinking a material can only be used for one thing.

faq.q: Why are different materials used for different things?
faq.a: Each material has properties that suit some jobs. Glass is transparent for windows; metal is strong for spoons; plastic is waterproof for raincoats.

faq.q: Can one material be used for lots of things?
faq.a: Yes. Wood is used for tables, pencils, doors and toys.

faq.q: How can I test if a material is waterproof?
faq.a: Drip the same amount of water onto each material. If the water stays on top and does not soak through, it is waterproof.
